_meta.purpose: Cap#165 wave 2 — plain-language summaries auto-injected at top of content pages by js/kid-mode.js. Add a key for each page (filename only, no path) with a 'title' and 'text' field. Text should be readable by a 5-year-old: short sentences, simple words, no jargon. Optional 'cta' object with 'label' + 'href' for a big call-to-action below the text.
_meta.audience: Adults who don't usually engage with legal/political prose. Tone: subtle talk-down — calibrated condescension that the reader notices but does not find cruel. Per Daniel directive 2026-04-26 + feedback_kid_mode_is_eli5_for_adults.md.
_meta.rule: Every claim in the kid summary must be true and supported by the page below it. Do not lose accuracy.
_meta.author: claude_code

maid-accountability.html.title: Plain English: The Death Program (MAID)
maid-accountability.html.text: Politicians in Canada made it legal for doctors to help sick people die. Yes, really — that's what they did. They called it MAID. At first they said it was only for people who were dying anyway. Then they expanded it. Soldiers who came home injured. People who couldn't afford food. People who couldn't pay rent. All of them now eligible. Read that twice if it didn't land the first time. The full page below names every politician who voted for this, with the actual votes and transcripts.

follow-the-money.html.title: Plain English: Where the Money Went
follow-the-money.html.text: Canada's government runs on tax money — your money — meant for hospitals, schools, soldiers, and people who can't work. Some politicians and their friends kept money that was meant for those things. They moved it to companies they own, to friends, to themselves. The amounts are bigger than you think. The full page below shows where it went, with the receipts. We made it easy to follow on purpose.

petitions.html.title: Plain English: People Asked. Almost Nobody Listened.
petitions.html.text: When something the government does makes you angry, you can sign a petition. Other people sign too. The government has to formally read every petition. But almost every one gets the same boilerplate response: 'we acknowledge receipt of your petition, thank you.' That is the entire reply. Nothing changes. They count on you not noticing. The full page below has the petitions and the non-replies.

veterans.html.title: Plain English: The Soldiers Who Came Home
veterans.html.text: Canadians serve in the military. Some come home injured. They need a doctor, a wheelchair, a counsellor. Canada promised to take care of them. Instead, some veterans who asked for help were offered the death program (MAID). Yes, really. We know that's a lot. Some are still waiting for help. Some are not waiting anymore — they died waiting. The full page below has the names and the documents.

foreign-interference.html.title: Plain English: Foreign Help Decided Some Elections
foreign-interference.html.text: Candidates have to win an election to get into office in Canada. Every Canadian gets one vote. Highest count wins. But some candidates received help from foreign governments to win. That is illegal. The full page below names who, names the foreign country that helped them, and shows the evidence. The fact that no one's been charged is a separate problem.

history-deep.html.title: Plain English: What Happened, Year by Year
history-deep.html.text: A timeline. Each year has a short note about what the government did or did not do. Tap a year to read the entries for that year. The timeline starts decades ago and continues to today. The patterns repeat. Once you see them you'll see them everywhere — that's how it's supposed to work.

home.html.title: Plain English: Welcome
home.html.text: This is TENET5. It documents what the people in charge of Canada have done, with primary-source proof. Some of it is upsetting. All of it is real. Nothing here is invented. Every story is backed by a document, a transcript, a recording, or a video. We made the simple version one click away from every page so there's no excuse not to read it.

index.html.title: Plain English: What This Site Is
index.html.text: This front screen is dense. That's the OSINT dashboard for people who follow this work daily. If that's too much for you right now, the Plain English overview gives you the entire story in short sentences. We kept it short on purpose.

take-action.html.title: Plain English: What You Can Do
take-action.html.text: Three things anyone can do today. They take five minutes each. (1) Share this site with one person you know. One more reader is one more witness. (2) Email your MP — that's the politician your area sends to Parliament — they have to read constituent mail. (3) Read one detailed page from start to finish. Then tell someone what it says. The full page below has the email templates so you don't have to write your own.
